{{eastern name order|Jákli Antal}}
'''Antal I. "Tony" Jákli''' (born 3 October 1958) is a Hungarian-American [[physicist]] and professor of physics and materials science at [[Kent State University]]. He is known for his work with bent-core,<ref>{{cite journal|title = Evidence for Triclinic Symmetry in Smectic Liquid Crystals of Bent-Shape Molecules| author1 = Jákli, A.|author2 = Krüerke, D. |author3 = Sawade, H.| author4 = Heppke, G. | s2cid = 17126162| journal = Phys. Rev. Lett. | volume = 86 | issue = 25| pages = 5715–5718 | year = 2001|doi = 10.1103/physrevlett.86.5715 | pmid = 11415340| bibcode = 2001PhRvL..86.5715J}}</ref><ref name="Eremin Jákli 2013 pp. 615–637">{{cite journal | last1=Eremin | first1=A. | last2=Jákli | first2=A. | title=Polar bent-shape liquid crystals – from molecular bend to layer splay and chirality | journal=Soft Matter | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=9 | issue=3 | year=2013 | issn=1744-683X | doi=10.1039/c2sm26780b | pages=615–637| bibcode=2013SMat....9..615E }}</ref> flexoelectric, and ferroelectric [[liquid crystal]]s.

== Education and career ==
Jákli received a [[Master of Science]] in 1983 and a Ph.D. in 1986 in [[Physics]] from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in [[Budapest]], Hungary.<ref name="FacultyBio">{{cite web|url=http://www.kent.edu/cas/cpip/~ajakli/ |title=Antal Jakli, Department of Chemical Physics - Faculty |publisher=Kent State University |access-date=2014-03-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322082824/http://www.kent.edu/cas/cpip/~ajakli/ |archive-date=2014-03-22 }}</ref> After postdoctoral fellowships with [[Alfred Saupe]] at Kent State University (1989–1992) and at the [[Max Planck Institute]] in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]], Germany (1993–1995), he served as a research fellow at the Research Institute for Solid State Physics in Budapest. He was awarded a D.Sc. from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 2000.

In 1999, Jákli joined the [[Liquid Crystal Institute]] (now the Advanced Materials and Liquid Crystal Institute) at Kent State University as a research fellow. He was appointed assistant professor in 2004, received tenure in 2007, and was promoted to full professor in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antal Jakli {{!}} Advanced Materials and Liquid Crystal Institute |url=https://www.kent.edu/amlci/antal-jakli |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=www.kent.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Jákli's research focuses on the physical, electro-optical, and electromechanical properties of liquid crystals, particularly molecular systems with reduced symmetry. His work has significantly advanced the understanding of bent-core (or "banana-shaped") molecules, which exhibit polar and chiral phases that are absent in traditional rod-shaped liquid crystals. He is particularly recognized for his contributions to the study of "banana mania" in nematic phases and the characterization of the twist-bend nematic phase.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jákli |first1=A. |last2=Lavrentovich |first2=O. D. |last3=Selinger |first3=J. V. |title=Physics of liquid crystals of bent-shaped molecules |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=90 |issue=4 |article-number=045004 |year=2018 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.90.045004}}</ref>

His research also encompasses [[flexoelectricity]]—the coupling between polarization and strain—where he demonstrated "giant" flexoelectric effects in bent-core systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Harden |first1=J. |last2=Mbanga |first2=B. |last3=Éber |first3=N. |last4=Fodor-Csorba |first4=K. |last5=Sprunt |first5=S. |last6=Gleeson |first6=J. T. |last7=Jákli |first7=A. |title=Giant Flexoelectricity of Bent-Core Nematic Liquid Crystals |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=97 |issue=15 |article-number=157802 |year=2006 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.157802}}</ref> Since the emergence of the field in 2020, Jákli's research has extensively focused on ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Feng |first1=Chenrun |last2=Saha |first2=Rony |last3=Korblova |first3=Eva |last4=Walba |first4=David |last5=Sprunt |first5=Samuel N. |last6=Jákli |first6=Antal |date=2021 |title=Electrically Tunable Reflection Color of Chiral Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals |journal=Advanced Optical Materials |volume=9 |issue=22 |article-number=2101230 |doi=10.1002/adom.202101230 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Máthé |first1=Marcell Tibor |last2=Buka |first2=Ágnes |last3=Jákli |first3=Antal |last4=Salamon |first4=Péter |date=2022 |title=Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal thermo-motor |journal=Physical Review E |volume=105 |issue=5 |article-number=L052701 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.105.L052701 |arxiv=2201.07556 }}</ref> In 2024, his team reported the first demonstration of converse piezoelectricity in three-dimensional fluids using these materials, a discovery termed "liquid piezoelectricity" with potential applications in soft robotics and sensors.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Máthé |first1=M. T. |last2=Himel |first2=M. S. H. |last3=Adaka |first3=A. |last4=Gleeson |first4=J. T. |last5=Sprunt |first5=S. |last6=Salamon |first6=P. |last7=Jákli |first7=A. |title=Liquid Piezoelectric Materials: Linear Electromechanical Effect in Fluid Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals |journal=Advanced Functional Materials |volume=34 |issue=18 |article-number=2314158 |year=2024 |doi=10.1002/adfm.202314158}}</ref>

Additionally, he has developed responsive materials including ionic liquid crystal elastomers (iLCEs) and electrospun fibers for use in soft actuators.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Feng |first1=C. |last2=Rajapaksha |first2=C. P. H. |last3=Cedillo |first3=J. M. |last4=Lioi |first4=S. M. |last5=Pelter |first5=L. S. |last6=Gleeson |first6=J. T. |last7=Sprunt |first7=S. |last8=Jákli |first8=A. |title=Electroresponsive Ionic Liquid Crystal Elastomers |journal=Macromolecular Rapid Communications |volume=40 |issue=19 |article-number=1900299 |year=2019 |doi=10.1002/marc.201900299}}</ref> His interdisciplinary work also extends to biotechnology, where he has utilized thermotropic liquid crystal films as label-free biosensors for the detection of antigens and enzymatic activity.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Popov |first1=P. |last2=Honaker |first2=L. W. |last3=Kooijman |first3=E. E. |last4=Mann |first4=E. K. |last5=Jákli |first5=A. I. |title=A liquid crystal biosensor for specific detection of antigens |journal=Sensing and Bio-Sensing Research |volume=8 |pages=31–35 |year=2016 |doi=10.1016/j.sbsr.2016.03.003|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Awards ==
* [[Alfred Saupe Prize]] (2020), awarded by the German Liquid Crystal Society.<ref name="Saupe2020">{{cite news |title=Antal Jákli to Receive the Alfred Saupe Prize in 2020 |url=https://www.kent.edu/amlci/news/antal-jakli-receive-alfred-saupe-prize-2020-outstanding-work-science-and-application |work=Advanced Materials and Liquid Crystal Institute |date=17 January 2020 |access-date=13 May 2026}}</ref>
* Luckhurst-Samulski Prize (2010), for the paper "Electro-mechanical effects in liquid crystals" published in the journal ''Liquid Crystals''.<ref name="Luckhurst2010">{{cite journal |title=The 2010 Luckhurst–Samulski Prize |journal=Liquid Crystals |volume=38 |issue=3 |pages=253-254 |year=2011 |doi=10.1080/02678292.2011.565208}}</ref>
* Outstanding Research Scholar of Kent State University (2012)
* Bólyai Young Researchers Scholar (1998–1999), Hungarian Academy of Sciences
